question: Forced perspective, which makes the nearer actor look bigger, normally forbids camera moves. How did The Fellowship of the Ring move anyway?
options: Part of the set moved with the camera
Wide lenses hid the distance change
answer: Part of the set moved with the camera. When a camera moves, near and far things shift at different rates and the trick shows. Weta put one actor's section of the set on a motorised platform that moved with the camera, keeping the distances in proportion. Gandalf and Frodo could share moving shots.
move: When a trick breaks under movement, move part of the trick too.
trap: Assuming an epic released in 2001 did its moving shots digitally.
source: Sibley, The Making of the Movie Trilogy
reference: Sibley, The Lord of the Rings: The Making of the Movie Trilogy, Houghton Mifflin, 2002
